children.text: Shorter - 2-3 sentences. Less is more : ).
I'd appreciate from the downvoters how I can improve.

I'm a CS grad with some work experience (1 year dev, 1 year coding bootcamp teacher). See me as a junior that ramps up quicker than the average junior (e.g. last month I owned a lot of boxes at hackthebox.eu for fun and was a top 5% after 2 weeks of non-stop playing [1]).

I wrote my thesis related to Engelbard. So I think we have a cultural click. Which is why I'm writing all this.

The reason I'm not applying but simply writing things here is because I'm tired of applying (it's hard to hear more than 100+ "no" while at university you were a top student). But I do want to know if you guys think I'm worth considering.

Which is why I'm brutally honest with the following:

Companies tend to reject me due to lack of experience, and (in my opinion) undervalue how quick I can pick things up and how willing I am to work amazingly hard, especially at the beginning of a job. When they hire me they tend to be surprised with how wrong they were about me.

My strength is that I'm a generalist, much more so than most people. My weakness is that people have the perception that I can't be a specialist. But anyone that gave me a chance in hiring me during my freelance time know that I am capable of performing one role as a specialist (full-stack developer with a business and security mindset).

During my good days I tend to have an Elon Musk mindset. He says that working 80 to 100 hours per week means you learn 2 to 2.5 times faster, I mostly agree -- I think it is sometimes more because the interconnectness of things pushes the multiple a bit higher. During my bad days I simply want to work 40 hours per week go home and relax. During these times I sort of don't want to work due to stress, but know that I have to work because it keeps my mind sharp.

[1] I was in "Elon Musk" mode for a month.

raw.description:
Job Description Summary

The Asia Indirect Sourcing Manager is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies across indirect spend categories (e.g., IT, HR services, facilities, marketing, professional services) within the Asia region. This role drives cost optimization, supplier performance, and compliance with global procurement policies while supporting business growth and operational efficiency.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Develop and implement regional sourcing strategies aligned with global category strategies

  • Manage end-to-end sourcing (RFx, negotiation, contracting) across indirect categories

  • Identify cost-saving opportunities and deliver annual productivity targets

2. Supplier Management

  • Build and maintain strategic supplier relationships across Asia

  • Lead supplier evaluation, selection, and performance management (KPIs, SLAs)

  • Drive supplier innovation, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement

3. Stakeholder Engagement

  • Partner with business leaders (Finance, HR, IT, Operations) to understand requirements

  • Act as a trusted advisor to internal stakeholders on sourcing strategies and market insights

  • Manage cross-functional alignment across multiple countries

4. Contracting & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with company procurement policies and governance (e.g., Ariba, ERP systems)

  • Lead contract negotiations to secure favorable commercial and legal terms

  • Mitigate risks related to supply continuity, legal, and regulatory requirements

5. Regional Leadership

  • Manage sourcing activities across multiple Asia countries (SEA, India, China, etc.)

  • Drive standardization, process improvements, and best practices across the region

  • Support transformation initiatives (digital procurement, automation, analytics)

6. Financial & Performance Management

  • Deliver cost savings, cost avoidance, and value creation targets

  • Monitor spend analytics and identify optimization opportunities

  • Report sourcing performance to regional/global leadership

Key Categories

  • IT & Telecom

  • HR & Professional Services

  • Facilities Management

  • Marketing & Events

  • Travel & Living; Fleet

  • MRO

  • Labor & Engineering

  • Utilities

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, or related field (MBA preferred)

  • 8–15+ years of experience in sourcing/procurement, preferably in MNC environment

  • Strong experience in indirect sourcing and regional (Asia) exposure

  • Proven track record in cost savings and supplier negotiations

  • Experience with procurement tools (e.g., Ariba, SAP)

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong negotiation and influencing skills

  • Strategic thinking with hands-on execution capability

  • Stakeholder management across cultures and seniority levels

  • Analytical and data-driven decision-making

  • Excellent communication and leadership skills

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Cost savings / cost avoidance (%)

  • Supplier performance & compliance

  • Contract coverage

  • Stakeholder satisfaction

  • Cycle time for sourcing projects

Additional Information

Relocation Assistance Provided: No

- This is a remote position
